summary: Iteration 63 — Notification preferences (backend + frontend) end-to-end validated. 16/16 backend pytest cases pass and all 4 UI flows (settings card, mode toggles, snooze chip, AuthDeeplink redirect, NotificationSnooze success/error) work correctly.

minor.issue: Frontend clearSnooze() is a client-only optimistic no-op — there is no DELETE endpoint to un-snooze a category. Reload will re-render the chip until natural 7-day expiry. Author's comment (`NotificationSettings.jsx` line ~113) acknowledges this as a placeholder.

action_items: Optional: add a DELETE /marketplace/notification-preferences/snooze/{category} endpoint and wire NotificationSettings clearSnooze() to actually call it (currently the UI action is optimistic-only).
critical_code_review_comments: notification_prefs.py uses `os.environ['MONGO_URL']` at import time via a fresh AsyncIOMotorClient — this duplicates the shared client from routes.deps. Minor: consider importing `db` from routes.deps for consistency and connection reuse.

PatchIn already validates mode via Literal — the explicit `if payload.mode not in MODES: raise 400` inside patch_preferences is unreachable (pydantic will 422 before we get there). Harmless but dead code.

NotificationSettings.jsx clearSnooze is misleading — it does not hit the backend; on reload the chip returns. Either implement the DELETE endpoint or make it clear in the UI that this only clears locally.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (settings toggles, snooze chip, AuthDeeplink, NotificationSnooze all pass)

Deeplink + snooze consume are public token-signed endpoints (no bearer required); use utils.notification_tokens.create_deeplink_token / create_snooze_token with JWT_SECRET from backend .env to mint fresh tokens for tests.
